newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian crudes slightly down, light Gulf grades firm.
newsitem.headline: Asian crudes slightly down, light Gulf grades firm.

text.p: Crude oil prices were slightly weaker on Thursday following an overnight decline in futures prices, but differentials for light Gulf and some Indonesian grades were firmer.
Traders said December Murban was sold by a European major at ADNOC +46 cents per barrel to a U.S. major.
The two majors then exchanged a cargo of December Lower Zakum at ADNOC +55 cents, traders said.
These prices were 10 to 15 cents above price levels seen for November cargoes amid seasonal demand for light crudes yielding middle distillates.

Traders said 700,000 barrels of December Qatar Land were sold by a Japanese trader to a European major at QGPC +27 cents, seven cents per barrel higher than an earlier deal for December into South Korea.
The December Oman market was steady with traders reporting deals at MPM +4 cents and MPM +5 cents, steady compared to recent deals.
Strong demand for Duri crude pushed the premium to 50 cents per barrel on buying from a South Korea refiner.
Duri has again been trading for export out of Asia, although South Korean demand is rising with new refining capacity.

Indonesian allocations of export crude fell in November to 282,000 barrels per day (bpd) from October's 345,000 bpd. Duri allocation was again high at 80,000 barrels a day, accounting for the turnaround of the 125,000 bpd Balongan refinery which could last up to the middle of November. About 70 percent of the refinery's feedstock is Duri.
Dubai intermonth spreads were mostly steady at 50/55 cents for near months ahead of India's NOvember crude tender which is expected to be awarded on Friday.
